scenario: A ski-lift operations report logs daily rider counts only when they exceed 4,000. Resort managers want the average daily rider count across all days.

data.description: Only days above 4,000 riders are observed. Rider count is Normal with known sigma 1,000.

question: Estimate (a) the true mean daily rider count mu across all days and (b) the fraction of days represented in the report.
naive_answer: Average daily ridership is about 4,454 because that is the report mean.
reasoning_trace: Alpha≈1.4 gives mu=4000-1400=2600 and observed fraction about 0.0808.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(4000-mu)/1000; return mu+1000*norm.pdf(a)/norm.sf(a)-4454.0
mu=brentq(eq,-5000,3999)
frac=norm.sf((4000-mu)/1000)
assert abs(mu-2600)<60 and abs(frac-0.0808)<0.005
